comments.body:
### Capture the blur task state (1/2)

**Severity:** `high`

Removing and re-adding a monitor handle creates a new state while an older blur can still finish. Capture the scheduled state so completion can reject work for the old instance; the existing blur-failure recovery can remain unchanged.

```suggestion
            _ = Task.Run(() => this.RunBlur(screenInfo, state, screenshotImage));
```

Apply every suggestion in this numbered group together; individual members are not complete fixes.

comments.body:
### Keep a zero SendInput return as failure

**Severity:** `medium`

The full-count comparison now rejects partial insertion. It also accepts zero when pInputs is empty, although the documented zero return denotes failure and the previous wrapper rejected it. Require both a nonzero return and the complete requested count; preserve the native result and available last error.

```suggestion
        return result != 0 && result == (uint)pInputs.Length
            ? new Win32Result<uint>(result, success: true)
            : new Win32Result<uint>(result, success: false, lastError: Marshal.GetLastPInvokeError());
```
comments.title: Keep a zero SendInput return as failure
